docs.purpose: Shows the history of recent data-import runs that pull the City of Toronto's open permit data into the system, and lets an operator manually kick off a new import from a given file, updating and classifying permits as it goes.
docs.data_story: It reads 5 tables — `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades`, `permit_type_classifications` and `permits` and writes `sync_runs`, `permits`, `permit_trades` and `permit_history`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: No SPEC LINK header. POST dynamically imports src/lib/sync/process.ts (runSync) to avoid loading the sync machinery on every request. runSync processes each permit record in its own transaction so one bad record does not roll back the batch. Classified COMMAND because the endpoint's stated job is to trigger a sync run, though GET alone would be QUERY. No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: WHAT IT HONESTLY IS: a 53-line thin wrapper. GET is a raw `SELECT * FROM sync_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20` returned unprojected (:11-15). POST takes `{ file_path }`, dynamically imports `runSync` from src/lib/sync/process.ts (:42) and returns the finished sync_runs row. All real work — the 9 write statements and 5 reads enumerated above — lives in src/lib/sync/process.ts (404 lines, read in full). RISK a reviewer must know: POST performs a mass DB mutation across permits / permit_trades / permit_history with NO in-handler auth check and NO validation of file_path beyond truthiness (:32-39); the only gate is the middleware presence-check, which middleware.ts:84-89 itself documents as non-cryptographic. CENSUS AGREEMENT: the routes-index read/write table matches exactly. | Idempotency: NOT GUARDED at the route level. Every POST unconditionally INSERTs a new sync_runs row (src/lib/sync/process.ts:322-326) — there is no in-flight lock, advisory lock, dedup key or ON CONFLICT anywhere in the run lifecycle, so two concurrent or repeated POSTs with the same file_path start two concurrent full syncs. Downstream, the per-permit work is partially convergent: an unchanged content hash short-circuits to a last_seen_at touch (process.ts:209, :282-288) and permit_trades are DELETEd before re-INSERT (process.ts:261-264), but permit_history rows accumulate one set per run that observes a diff (process.ts:248-257), and sync_runs rows accumulate unconditionally. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-53) | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.
